title: "NFL Draft Predictor | Model 6 — Random Forest"
output: html_document

# Model 6 — Random Forest

Random Forest combines many Decision Trees to generate predictions. Unlike a single Decision Tree, it allows different variables and observations to influence each tree, helping reduce overfitting.

We compare two values of `mtry`, which determines how many predictors are considered at each split. To keep computation manageable, we use 3-fold cross-validation on a representative sample of up to 2,500 historical players. We select the model with the highest Kappa, then train our final Random Forest on the complete historical training dataset.

The 2022–2025 test data is not used during model tuning.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

dir.create("objects", showWarnings = FALSE)

# Load the prepared data from File 01.
train_x_raw <- readRDS("objects/train_x_raw.rds")
test_x_raw <- readRDS("objects/test_x_raw.rds")
train_y <- readRDS("objects/train_y.rds")
```

## Step 1: Prepare a smaller tuning sample

```{r tuning-sample}
library(caret)
library(randomForest)

# Limit the cross-validation sample to 2,500 players.
# We preserve the proportion of drafted and undrafted players.
set.seed(12345)

rf_n <- min(2500, length(train_y))

if (rf_n < length(train_y)) {
  tune_rows <- as.vector(
    createDataPartition(
      train_y,
      p = rf_n / length(train_y),
      list = FALSE
    )
  )
} else {
  tune_rows <- seq_along(train_y)
}

rf_tune_x <- train_x_raw[tune_rows, , drop = FALSE]
rf_tune_y <- train_y[tune_rows]

cat("Players used for tuning:", nrow(rf_tune_x), "\n")
cat("Players available for final training:", nrow(train_x_raw), "\n")
```

## Step 2: Tune the Random Forest

```{r tuning}
# mtry controls the number of variables considered at each split.
p <- ncol(train_x_raw)

mtry_values <- unique(
  pmin(p, c(2, floor(sqrt(p))))
)

# Use three folds and two mtry candidates to reduce training time.
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 3,
  classProbs = FALSE,
  verboseIter = TRUE,
  allowParallel = FALSE
)

set.seed(12345)

rf_tuned <- train(
  x = rf_tune_x,
  y = rf_tune_y,
  method = "rf",
  tuneGrid = expand.grid(mtry = mtry_values),
  ntree = 80,
  nodesize = 10,
  trControl = ctrl,
  metric = "Kappa",
  importance = FALSE
)

# Save the cross-validation results for the final report.
rf_cv <- rf_tuned$results

print(rf_cv)
print(rf_tuned$bestTune)

# Select the mtry value with the highest cross-validation Kappa.
best_mtry <- as.integer(rf_tuned$bestTune$mtry)
```

## Step 3: Train the Final Random Forest

```{r final-model}
# Refit the model using ALL historical training players.
# The future-year test dataset remains untouched.

cat("Fitting final Random Forest using mtry =", best_mtry, "\n")

set.seed(12345)

rf_model <- randomForest(
  x = train_x_raw,
  y = train_y,
  mtry = best_mtry,
  ntree = 150,
  nodesize = 10,
  importance = TRUE
)

print(rf_model)

# Random Forest also reports its out-of-bag error.
# This provides an additional training-based performance check.
cat("Final out-of-bag error:\n")
print(tail(rf_model$err.rate, 1))

# Show which variables contribute most to predictions.
varImpPlot(
  rf_model,
  main = "Random Forest Variable Importance"
)
```

## Step 4: Predict the Test Data

```{r predictions}
# Predict the probability of being drafted for each test player.
rf_prob <- as.numeric(
  predict(
    rf_model,
    newdata = test_x_raw,
    type = "prob"
  )[, "Drafted"]
)

# Convert probabilities to Drafted / Undrafted classifications.
rf_pred <- factor(
  ifelse(rf_prob >= 0.5, "Drafted", "Undrafted"),
  levels = c("Undrafted", "Drafted")
)

# Verify that every test player received a valid probability.
stopifnot(
  length(rf_prob) == nrow(test_x_raw),
  all(is.finite(rf_prob)),
  all(rf_prob >= 0 & rf_prob <= 1)
)

cat("Test predictions generated:", length(rf_pred), "\n")
print(table(rf_pred))
```

## Step 5: Save Results

```{r save-results, include=FALSE}
# Preserve the same object filenames used by later project files.
saveRDS(rf_model, "objects/rf_model.rds")
saveRDS(rf_cv, "objects/rf_cv.rds")
saveRDS(rf_prob, "objects/rf_prob.rds")
saveRDS(rf_pred, "objects/rf_pred.rds")
```
